Bharti Airtel shares jump after Q2 show; CLSA hikes target, HSBC maintains Buy; check fresh targets
sum: Shares of Bharti Airtel Ltd rose over 2 per cent on Friday, November 6, after the telecom major reported a 31 per cent year-on-year (YoY) increase in consolidated net profit for the September quarter (Q2FY27).

The stock was trading at Rs 2,101.40 on the NSE, up Rs 44.50 or 2.16 per cent. It opened at Rs 2,120 and touched an intraday high of Rs 2,120 and a low of Rs 2,076.20. The company's market capitalisation stood at around Rs 12.58 lakh crore.
Bharti Airtel announced its Q2 results after market hours on Thursday.
The company's consolidated net profit rose to Rs 8,887.5 crore in Q2FY27, compared with Rs 6,791.6 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Revenue from operations increased 16.7 per cent YoY to Rs 60,878 crore from Rs 52,145 crore in Q2FY26.

Operating performance also remained strong. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) grew 17.8 per cent YoY to Rs 35,240 crore from Rs 29,919 crore in the year-ago quarter.

India revenue increased 9.4 per cent YoY to Rs 42,308 crore. The mobile business continued to benefit from premiumisation, higher average revenue per user (ARPU) and additions in smartphone data customers.

sum: HSBC said it had revised its expectations for margin expansion in India and now sees international operations as a larger growth opportunity than it had previously anticipated. The brokerage has retained its valuation multiple for India while assigning a higher multiple to the international business.

Shares of Lenskart Solutions Ltd. opened with gains of over 6% on Thursday, November 5, after several brokerages maintained or upgraded their positive stance on the company following its strong September quarter (Q2 FY27) performance.

Nomura has maintained a 'Buy' rating on Lenskart with a price target of ₹888, while HSBC has upgraded the stock to 'Buy' and raised its price target to ₹790. CLSA has an 'Outperform' rating with a target of ₹773, while Jefferies has maintained its 'Buy' rating with a price target of ₹780.

Nomura said Lenskart's Q2 FY27 performance was ahead of estimates, with consolidated sales growing 32.5% year-on-year. EBITDA, before accounting for Ind AS 116, increased 65% year-on-year, while the corresponding margin expanded 270 basis points to 13.8%, supported by operating leverage across both India and international operations.

In India, strong same-store sales growth, in-house manufacturing and rental leverage supported margin improvement. International operations also delivered volume-led growth, with pre-Ind AS EBITDA margins remaining in double digits.
The brokerage highlighted several initiatives aimed at driving long-term volume growth of 20% and achieving an operating margin of 25%.

HSBC upgraded Lenskart to 'Buy' and raised its price target to ₹790. The brokerage said that EBITDA was 3% ahead of consensus estimates, with India same-store sales growth at 21% and international operations sustaining growth of 23% in constant currency terms.

items.t: HSBC stock: Q3 profit jumps as buyback and outlook hold
sum: HSBC Holdings reported stronger third-quarter results on October 27, 2026, while keeping its financial targets unchanged. In its 3Q26 earnings release, the bank said profit before tax increased 32 percent from a year earlier to 9.6 billion US dollars.

The headline increase included a favorable 1.4 billion US dollar effect from notable items, mainly because legal provisions recorded in the third quarter of 2025 did not recur. Excluding notable items, constant-currency profit before tax rose by 0.9 billion US dollars to 10.0 billion US dollars. Profit after tax increased 38 percent to 7.6 billion US dollars.

Revenue rose 0.8 billion US dollars to 18.6 billion US dollars, driven mainly by banking net interest income. HSBC also cited higher fee and other income in Corporate and Institutional Banking, Wealth and other businesses. Revenue excluding notable items on a constant-currency basis increased to 18.7 billion US dollars.

Net interest income advanced 6 percent to 9.3 billion US dollars, while banking net interest income increased by 0.6 billion US dollars to 11.7 billion US dollars. The net interest margin held steady at 1.57 percent. Expected credit losses fell 17 percent to 0.8 billion US dollars, although the bank continued to monitor commercial real estate and other credit exposures.

HSBC stock traded at 15.75 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:47 CET on Wednesday, November 4, 4.30 percent above the Xetra close of Tuesday, November 3, at 15.10 euros. Investors can follow the real-time quote of HSBC stock.

The board approved a third interim dividend of 0.10 US dollars per share. HSBC completed a 1 billion US dollar buyback on September 28 and intends to start another repurchase of up to 1 billion US dollars, which it expects to complete by the announcement of its 2026 full-year results.

Management retained its target for banking net interest income of at least 46 billion US dollars in 2026. It also maintained a return on average tangible equity target of 17 percent or better for 2026 through 2028, excluding notable items, and a 50 percent dividend payout ratio target through 2028.

sum: HSBC upgraded Megacable to Buy on October 13, 2026, and lifted its price target to MXN 75.00 from MXN 67.00. The move gives investors a fresh valuation reference for the Mexican cable and communications group.
The upgrade and target change are listed by Investing.com. The financial website also shows a consensus rating of Buy based on 13 analysts, including nine Buy ratings, four Holds and one Sell.

The average 12-month analyst target is MXN 70.238, while the published range extends from MXN 52.10 to MXN 84.00. HSBC stock heads into Dubai finance forum after strong quarter
sum: HSBC stock enters the week of Monday, November 2, with HSBC Asset Management CEO Nicolas Moreau listed among the speakers at Dubai Future Finance Week. The event runs from November 2 to 6 and will bring together financial institutions, investors and policymakers, according to Fast Company Middle East.

The program includes more than 85 events, 12 flagship forums and more than 850 expected speakers. The Dubai FinTech Summit on November 2 and 3 is the week's main event, while later sessions focus on sustainable finance, Islamic finance, private capital and tokenized markets.

HSBC's latest operating update provides the financial context for the conference appearance. The bank reported third-quarter revenue of 18.7 billion US dollars and profit before tax of 10.0 billion US dollars excluding notable items for the period ended September 30, 2026. Annualised return on tangible equity reached 18.8 percent year to date, also excluding notable items, according to HSBC Investors.

Management reiterated its medium-term targets, including revenue growth of 5 percent by 2028, return on tangible equity of 17 percent or better and dividends equal to 50 percent of earnings per share, subject to the stated exclusions. The bank also approved a third interim dividend of 10 US cents per share for 2026.

HSBC stock traded at 15.22 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 17:00:33 CET on Sunday, November 1, 0.78 percent below the Xetra close of Friday, October 30, at 15.34 euros. The real-time quote of HSBC stock reflects the Sunday trading snapshot.

HSBC shares slide almost 7% as revenue misses and wealth stalls despite 32% profit jump
sum: - HSBC reported third-quarter results on Tuesday, October 27, and the shares fell almost 7% even though profit rose sharply.

- HSBC shares fell almost 7% after Q3 revenue of around $18.6bn missed forecasts and wealth revenue stalled, overshadowing a 32% jump in pre-tax profit to around $9.6bn and a fresh buyback of up to $1bn. Guidance was only reaffirmed, not upgraded.

The sell-off shows how much was already priced into HSBC after a strong run. Without a guidance upgrade, a revenue miss and stalled wealth growth were enough to trigger profit-taking. The read-across for Hong Kong and Asian banks is margin pressure: costlier time deposits threaten interest income just as the Fed’s hiking path keeps funding costs high. Oil matters indirectly, since inflation and rate uncertainty linked to the Iran war is weighing on bank valuations broadly, and HSBC is already setting aside provisions for the Middle East conflict. The Basel 3.1 capital boost from January 2027 gives HSBC room to expand buybacks, which could limit further downside once the disappointment fades.
HSBC delivered a big profit jump and another $1 billion buyback, but a revenue miss, flat wealth income and no upgrade to its targets were enough to send the shares sharply lower.
- HSBC shares fell almost 7% on Tuesday after third-quarter revenue of around $18.6 billion missed forecasts of roughly $19.1 billion, and adjusted EPS of $2.10 missed $2.22.
- Pre-tax profit rose 32% to around $9.6 billion, helped by the absence of last year’s legal provisions. Excluding notable items, it rose about 10% to around $10 billion.
- Wealth revenue was flat at around $2.7 billion after strong growth in the first half. Net interest income rose 6% but was slightly below expectations.

Top Utilities Stocks to Watch: HSBC’s Preferred Picks
sum: Investing.com -- HSBC has identified five preferred utilities stocks positioned to benefit from surging electricity demand driven by data centers and artificial intelligence infrastructure. The investment bank rates all five companies as Buy, citing above-average growth prospects and strong execution capabilities in an evolving power landscape.

The utilities sector is experiencing a transformation as electricity demand accelerates, particularly in regions attracting large data center developments. HSBC's preferred stocks demonstrate rate base growth rates well above historical averages, with several companies projecting demand increases of 40% to 80% by 2030. The bank's selections span integrated electric utilities, transmission-focused operators, and diversified energy infrastructure companies across multiple U.S. markets.

1. Entergy (ETR) - HSBC rates Entergy as Buy with a target price of USD123.50, implying 17.5% upside. The integrated electric utility operates in Louisiana, Arkansas, Texas, Mississippi and New Orleans. HSBC forecasts 2026-30 rate base growth of 16% and earnings per share growth of 13%. The company's USD67 billion investment plan for 2026-30 includes plans to add approximately 30GW of new capacity through 2035. Louisiana drives growth with approximately 60% demand increase expected by 2030. HSBC considers execution risk low, citing the company's early supply chain management and standardized processes.

2. Pinnacle West (PNW) - HSBC rates Pinnacle West as Buy with a target price of USD119.50, implying 15.5% upside. The Arizona-based integrated utility is forecasted to achieve 2026-30 rate base growth of 12% and earnings per share growth of 13%. The company has recorded growth rates of 5% to 10% in the last six quarters and forecasts approximately 45% demand increase by 2030. HSBC notes execution risk as medium to high due to past regulatory challenges, but expects material improvements following a pivotal ratemaking decision before year-end 2026.

3. NextEra (NEE) - HSBC rates NextEra as Buy with a target price of USD103.00, implying 29.1% upside. The company targets capital expenditures of USD295-325 billion over 2025-32, with USD185-225 billion allocated to NextEra Energy Resources.

sum: Chevron stock (ISIN US1667641005) was trading at EUR 180.53 at Lang & Schwarz on September 30, 2026 at 12:44 p.m. CEST, up 0.27 percent from the prior close of EUR 180.05. The main new company-specific signal is HSBC's higher valuation call, while Chevron's latest quarterly revenue also exceeded expectations.

According to Investing.com on September 25, 2026, HSBC raised its Chevron target from USD 218.00 to USD 250.00 and maintained a Buy rating. The USD 32.00 increase reflects Chevron's sensitivity to higher oil prices, although HSBC also identified lower 2027 US natural gas assumptions as a negative offset.

The new target is USD 250.00, while the primary exchange price was last at USD 204.39 on the NYSE on September 29, 2026 at 3:59 p.m. ET. That comparison puts the target USD 45.61 above the latest primary-exchange quote, but the reference price for this article remains the euro quote from Lang & Schwarz.

MarketBeat reported that Chevron's latest quarter delivered revenue of USD 67.20 billion, versus analyst estimates of USD 62.72 billion. The same report put adjusted EPS at USD 6.06, compared with consensus of USD 5.55, a USD 0.51 beat.

Chevron's revenue was up 57.4 percent from the same quarter a year earlier, according to MarketBeat. The scale of that increase matters because the integrated energy group remains highly exposed to upstream commodity prices, while its refining and distribution operations provide a second earnings channel.

Chevron's latest production update cited by Yahoo Finance showed global output of 4.07 million barrels of oil equivalent per day, up 20.00 percent year over year. That growth gives the HSBC target a tangible operating foundation, but it also leaves cash generation sensitive to oil and gas prices.

Chevron's market capitalization was USD 407.1 billion on September 29, 2026. Its 52-week range was USD 146.49 to USD 217.78, placing the primary-exchange quote USD 13.39 below the high and showing that the stock remains near the upper end of its annual range.

HSBC Stock Stalls as $1 Billion Buyback Disappoints Investors
sum: HSBC Holdings (NYSE:HSBC), one of the world's largest banks with a dominant franchise across Asia, barely moved in Tuesday afternoon trading in Hong Kong despite posting another earnings beat. First-half pretax profit jumped 23% year over year to $19.5 billion, comfortably ahead of the $18.9 billion analysts had expected. The bank also restarted capital returns with a new share-buyback program worth up to $1 billion after sitting on the sidelines for the past three quarters. Investors, however, were clearly looking for more.
- Is HSBC fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The first-half report had plenty of positives beneath the surface. HSBC raised its full-year net interest income guidance and now expects the figure to exceed $46 billion, up from its previous forecast of around that level. Wealth management continued firing on all cylinders, with revenue climbing 18% as affluent clients across Asia remained active. HSBC and Hang Seng Bank added roughly 640,000 new customers in Hong Kong during the period, while Corporate and Institutional Banking overtook every other division to contribute about one-third of the group's first-half profit. Management also revealed that more than 70 Asian IPOs are currently sitting in its deal pipeline, highlighting that capital-markets activity is beginning to recover across the region.

The attached GF Value chart adds another angle investors shouldn't ignore. While HSBC continues to deliver resilient earnings growth, GuruFocus estimates the stock's GF Value at $56.38 versus a recent market price of $106.32. That places the shares nearly 89% above their estimated intrinsic value and firmly in the "Significantly Overvalued" range. Strong businesses can stay expensive for long periods, but lofty valuations also leave less room for disappointment if growth slows.

That valuation backdrop helps explain why the stock failed to rally despite the earnings beat. HSBC shares retreated from their record high of HK$169.50 after investors focused on the size of the buyback instead. Citi analysts noted that the $1 billion repurchase authorization came in well below the roughly $2.2 billion the market had been expecting, overshadowing a pretax profit beat of around $600 million.

HSBC earnings beat estimates, company resumes stock buybacks
sum: HSBC Holdings reported first-half pretax profit of $19.5 billion on Tuesday, a 23% increase from a year earlier, as revenue growth in lending and wealth management drove earnings past analyst estimates.

Analysts had penciled in $18.9 billion, according to Reuters, making the result a beat. Profit after tax came in at $15.3 billion, up $2.9 billion from the first half of 2025. Revenue rose 11% to $37.7 billion.

Alongside the results, the bank announced it would restart share buybacks with a program capped at $1 billion, targeted for completion ahead of its third-quarter reporting date. The pause stretched across three quarters, tracing back to an October announcement that HSBC would acquire full ownership of Hang Seng Bank. That transaction closed in January at a price of nearly $14 billion, according to The Wall Street Journal.

"We delivered strong returns to our shareholders," Chief Executive Georges Elhedery said in a statement. "Our 18.2% annualised RoTE reflects a strong performance. We are paying another 10 cents per share quarterly interim dividend. We have also resumed share buy-backs (up to $1bn), three quarters after we paused them following the Hang Seng Bank privatisation announcement."
The board approved a second interim dividend of $0.10 per share, bringing the full first-half dividend to $0.20.

HSBC raised its banking net interest income guidance for 2026 to at least $46 billion, up from a prior forecast of around $46 billion, citing a continued favorable interest rate environment. Banking net interest income for the first half rose $1.6 billion to $22.9 billion, driven by deposit balance growth and the benefit of reinvestment of the bank's structural hedge at higher yields.

Wealth fee and other income grew 18% on a constant currency basis in the period. The corporate and institutional banking segment also posted growth, with wholesale transaction banking fee and other income rising 6% from a year earlier.
